title: Playbook Check CLI Commands (BLD-678)
description: This tour walks through the addition of the `hlx playbook` command group to the helix-cli. Two new subcommands are introduced: `hlx playbook check <rule-ref>` (which POSTs to trigger a playbook rule check, then polls GET until a terminal state is reached) and `hlx playbook checks <rule-ref>` (which lists check history for a rule). The implementation follows the existing `goals/` command group pattern: a router index, individual command modules, and a new case in the top-level dispatcher. The polling loop is a first for the CLI — no prior command waited for an async result.

steps.description: The top-level CLI dispatcher is the entry point for every `hlx` command. A new import for the `playbook` command group router is added here, mirroring the existing `goals` import directly above it. This is purely additive — nothing existing is modified.
steps.title: Step 1 — Top-level dispatcher: import

steps.description: A new `playbook` case is added to the main switch statement using the same `configOrHelp` pattern as the `goals` case. When the user types `hlx playbook ...`, execution is handed off to `src/playbook/index.ts`. Exit codes and error propagation are handled identically to every other command group — no special-casing needed.
steps.title: Step 2 — Top-level dispatcher: playbook case

steps.description: This file is the router for all `hlx playbook` subcommands. It mirrors `src/goals/index.ts` exactly: a switch statement dispatches on the first positional argument, falling through to a help text display for unknown or missing subcommands. `parseApiError` is imported from `goals/utils.ts` (shared utility) for user-friendly error messages. The two registered subcommands are `check` and `checks`. This pattern keeps the top-level dispatcher clean and makes adding future subcommands trivial.
steps.title: Step 3 — Playbook command group router

steps.description: The file opens by declaring the three key constants that govern polling: `POLL_INTERVAL_MS = 5_000` (5 seconds between polls), `MAX_POLLS = 120` (capping total wait at 10 minutes), and `TERMINAL_STATUSES = new Set(['PASS', 'FAIL', 'ERROR'])`. The `CheckRecord` type mirrors the server's `PlaybookRuleCheck` model fields, ensuring type-safe access to `status`, `interpretation`, `complianceRate`, `compliantCount`, `violatingCount`, `totalCount`, and `examples`. This is the first polling pattern introduced to the CLI — all values were chosen deliberately in the ticket spec.
steps.title: Step 4 — check.ts: constants and CheckRecord type

steps.description: The command first resolves the rule-ref argument to a rule ID, then POSTs to `/playbook/rules/${ruleId}/check` with `basePath: '/api'`. The `basePath` matches the server's `/api` router prefix used by every other CLI command. The response immediately returns a check object; if its status is already terminal (e.g., a GENERAL org ERROR), the function prints the result and exits without entering the poll loop. This handles the edge case where the check fails instantly.
steps.title: Step 5 — check.ts: POST to trigger the check

steps.description: After a non-terminal initial response, the command enters a `for` loop bounded by `MAX_POLLS`. Each iteration sleeps `POLL_INTERVAL_MS` milliseconds, then GETs `/playbook/rules/${ruleId}/checks/${check.id}`. If the returned status is in `TERMINAL_STATUSES`, the loop breaks and the result is printed. If the loop exhausts all iterations, a timeout message is printed and the process exits with code 1. Exit code 0 is reserved for PASS only — FAIL and ERROR also produce exit code 1, enabling CI integration.
steps.title: Step 6 — check.ts: GET poll loop

steps.description: This module handles `hlx playbook checks <rule-ref>`. It GETs `/playbook/rules/${ruleId}/checks` and renders a formatted table with columns: ID (truncated), Status, Compliance rate, and Checked At timestamp. An empty list is handled gracefully with a friendly message. The `--json` flag bypasses formatting and emits raw JSON to stdout, matching the pattern in `goals/list.ts`. This command is read-only and has no side effects.
steps.title: Step 7 — checks.ts: list check history

steps.description: All changes are strictly additive: three new files (`src/playbook/index.ts`, `src/playbook/check.ts`, `src/playbook/checks.ts`) and one new switch case plus one import in `src/index.ts`. No existing command group, utility, or type is modified. The new `playbook` command group follows the established `goals/` pattern throughout, meaning any developer familiar with `goals` can immediately read and extend `playbook`. The polling loop is self-contained in `check.ts` and does not affect any other command's execution path.
steps.title: Step 8 — Summary: clean code paths
